Compare the leftmost and rightmost heights of a subtree. Equal heights identify a perfect subtree with 2^h - 1 nodes; otherwise recurse into its children, exploiting completeness so most subtrees can be counted at once.

  • Only the first slot of the final level is occupied.

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0200-0299/0226.Invert%20Binary%20Tree/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def invertTree(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> Optional[TreeNode]:
        if root is None:
            return None
        l, r = self.invertTree(root.left), self.invertTree(root.right)
        root.left, root.right = r, l
        return root

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0200-0299/0230.Kth%20Smallest%20Element%20in%20a%20BST/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def kthSmallest(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], k: int) -> int:
        stk = []
        while root or stk:
            if root:
                stk.append(root)
                root = root.left
            else:
                root = stk.pop()
                k -= 1
                if k == 0:
                    return root.val
                root = root.right

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0200-0299/0234.Palindrome%20Linked%20List/Solution.py

# Definition for singly-linked list.
# class ListNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.next = next
class Solution:
    def isPalindrome(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> bool:
        slow, fast = head, head.next
        while fast and fast.next:
            slow, fast = slow.next, fast.next.next
        pre, cur = None, slow.next
        while cur:
            t = cur.next
            cur.next = pre
            pre, cur = cur, t
        while pre:
            if pre.val != head.val:
                return False
            pre, head = pre.next, head.next
        return True

#     def __init__(self, x):

class Solution:
    def lowestCommonAncestor(
        self, root: "TreeNode", p: "TreeNode", q: "TreeNode"
    ) -> "TreeNode":
        if root in (None, p, q):
            return root
        left = self.lowestCommonAncestor(root.left, p, q)
        right = self.lowestCommonAncestor(root.right, p, q)
        return root if left and right else (left or right)

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0200-0299/0238.Product%20of%20Array%20Except%20Self/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def productExceptSelf(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        ans = [0] * n
        left = right = 1
        for i, x in enumerate(nums):
            ans[i] = left
            left *= x
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            ans[i] *= right
            right *= nums[i]
        return ans

cards.title: Meeting Rooms II
cards.summary: Find the minimum number of rooms needed to host all meetings without conflicts within a room.
cards.question:
Find the minimum number of rooms needed to host all meetings without conflicts within a room.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Sort start times and end times separately, then sweep through their events. Allocate a room for a start before the next end, and free a room before processing a simultaneous start; the peak occupancy is the answer.

Target complexity

O(n log n) time and O(n) space for the sorted start/end arrays.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • No meetings → 0 rooms
  • Back-to-back meetings can share one room
  • Three simultaneous meetings need three rooms

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0200-0299/0253.Meeting%20Rooms%20II/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def minMeetingRooms(self, intervals: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        m = max(e[1] for e in intervals)
        d = [0] * (m + 1)
        for l, r in intervals:
            d[l] += 1
            d[r] -= 1
        ans = s = 0
        for v in d:
            s += v
            ans = max(ans, s)
        return ans

Prefix each string with its length and a separator, then concatenate the payloads. During decoding, parse a length first and consume exactly that many characters, so separators inside the payload remain ordinary data.

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0200-0299/0271.Encode%20and%20Decode%20Strings/Solution.py

class Codec:
    def encode(self, strs: List[str]) -> str:
        """Encodes a list of strings to a single string."""
        ans = []
        for s in strs:
            ans.append("{:4}".format(len(s)) + s)
        return "".join(ans)

    def decode(self, s: str) -> List[str]:
        """Decodes a single string to a list of strings."""
        ans = []
        i, n = 0, len(s)
        while i < n:
            size = int(s[i : i + 4])
            i += 4
            ans.append(s[i : i + size])
            i += size
        return ans

# codec = Codec()
# codec.decode(codec.encode(strs))

Maintain a write position for the next nonzero value and scan the array once. Compact nonzero values in order, then fill the remaining suffix with zeroes, or use swaps that preserve the same prefix invariant.

O(n) time and O(1) extra space; operate on the original array.

cards.title: Find the Duplicate Number
cards.summary: Find the repeated value in an array of n+1 values drawn from 1 through n, without modifying the array.
cards.question:
Find the repeated value in an array of n+1 values drawn from 1 through n, without modifying the array.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Treat each array value as the next index in a functional graph. Floyd’s cycle detection finds a meeting point, then resetting one pointer to index zero and advancing both one step identifies the cycle entrance, which is the duplicate value.

Target complexity

O(n) time and O(1) space; depends on the stated index range and exactly one repeated value.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • [1,1] → 1
  • [3,1,3,4,2] → 3
  • [2,2,2,2,2] → 2

cards.title: Game of Life
cards.summary: Compute one simultaneous update of a cellular grid using each cell’s eight neighbors.
cards.question:
Compute one simultaneous update of a cellular grid using each cell’s eight neighbors.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Encode both the old and new state in each cell while making the first pass. Count neighbors using only the old-state bit, write the next-state bit from the birth and survival rules, then discard the old bit in a second pass.

Target complexity

O(rows × columns) time and O(1) extra space with bit encoding; copying the board instead requires O(rows × columns) space.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • An isolated live cell dies.
  • A dead cell with exactly three live neighbors is born.
  • Border cells have fewer than eight neighbors.

cards.question:
Support inserting numbers and querying the median of all values seen so far.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Keep the lower half in a max heap and the upper half in a min heap. Preserve cross-heap ordering and rebalance sizes to differ by at most one, so one root or the average of two roots determines the median.

Target complexity

O(log n) insertion, O(1) median query, and O(n) space; median queries occur only after an insertion.

  • [-1,2] → median 0.5
  • Repeated equal values must remain separate observations

cards.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
cards.summary: Design a serialization format that reconstructs a binary tree’s values and exact shape.
cards.question:
Design a serialization format that reconstructs a binary tree’s values and exact shape.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Write a preorder stream containing both node values and explicit null markers. Decode by consuming one token at a time and recursively constructing exactly two children for each non-null token.

Target complexity

O(n) tokens and O(h) stack with an advancing cursor; serialized size also includes digit lengths. Repeatedly removing the first token from an array can make decoding O(n²).

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • Empty tree needs an unambiguous representation
  • Left-only and right-only trees must encode differently
  • Negative and multi-digit values must round-trip

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0200-0299/0297.Serialize%20and%20Deserialize%20Binary%20Tree/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode(object):
#     def __init__(self, x):
#         self.val = x
#         self.left = None
#         self.right = None


class Codec:
    def serialize(self, root):
        """Encodes a tree to a single string.

        :type root: TreeNode
        :rtype: str
        """
        if root is None:
            return ""
        q = deque([root])
        ans = []
        while q:
            node = q.popleft()
            if node:
                ans.append(str(node.val))
                q.append(node.left)
                q.append(node.right)
            else:
                ans.append("#")
        return ",".join(ans)

    def deserialize(self, data):
        """Decodes your encoded data to tree.

        :type data: str
        :rtype: TreeNode
        """
        if not data:
            return None
        vals = data.split(",")
        root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
        q = deque([root])
        i = 1
        while q:
            node = q.popleft()
            if vals[i] != "#":
                node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
                q.append(node.left)
            i += 1
            if vals[i] != "#":
                node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
                q.append(node.right)
            i += 1
        return root


# Your Codec object will be instantiated and called as such:
# codec = Codec()
# codec.deserialize(codec.serialize(root))

cards.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
cards.summary: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence, whose chosen elements need not be adjacent.
cards.question:
Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence, whose chosen elements need not be adjacent.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

A direct DP records the best subsequence starting at each position by testing later larger values. For an O(n log n) target, maintain the smallest possible tail for each subsequence length and binary-search the first tail not smaller than the new value.

Target complexity

Pairwise DP: O(n²) time/O(n) space. Binary-search tails: O(n log n) time/O(n) space; equal values replace rather than extend.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

  • [2,2,2] → 1
  • [5,4,3] → 1
  • [10,9,2,5,3,7,101,18] → 4

cards.question:
Find all roots that minimize the height of a given undirected tree.

Tree centers remain after repeatedly removing all current leaves together. Track degrees, peel one layer at a time, and stop when at most two vertices remain; those vertices minimize the greatest distance to any other vertex.

cards.question:
Count connected components in an undirected graph, including vertices with no edges.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Start with one component per vertex and union the endpoints of each edge. Decrease the component count only when two different representatives merge, or count distinct representatives after all edges are processed.

Target complexity

With union by rank and path compression: O((V+E)·α(V)) time/O(V) space; DFS is O(V+E). Both union balancing and path compression are needed for the stated amortized DSU bound.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

  • n isolated vertices → n components
  • A connected cycle → one component
  • An edge inside an existing component must not decrement twice

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0300-0399/0328.Odd%20Even%20Linked%20List/Solution.py

# Definition for singly-linked list.
# class ListNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.next = next
class Solution:
    def oddEvenList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if head is None:
            return None
        a = head
        b = c = head.next
        while b and b.next:
            a.next = b.next
            a = a.next
            b.next = a.next
            b = b.next
        a.next = c
        return head

cards.question:

Treat tickets as directed multigraph edges and apply an Eulerian-path traversal, consuming destinations in lexical order. Append an airport only after its outgoing tickets are exhausted, then reverse the postorder result so early dead ends land in the correct final position.

Target complexity

O(E log E) time/O(E) space using sorted adjacency with end-pops; avoid repeated front-pops and list copies.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • Duplicate tickets must be consumed separately
  • A lexically smallest next airport can be an immediate dead end
  • The final itinerary has one more airport than tickets

cards.question:
Return the population count of every integer from zero through n.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Reuse a smaller already-computed integer instead of counting each value from scratch. Removing the highest set power of two adds one bit to the earlier result, or equivalently use bits[i>>1] plus the low bit.

cards.question:
Implement posting, following, unfollowing, and a feed containing the ten newest tweets from a user and their followees.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Keep each user’s posts in timestamp order and store follow relationships in sets. Seed a heap with each relevant user’s newest post, then merge backward through those histories until ten tweets have been emitted.

Target complexity

Expected O(1) posting/follow updates; feed O(F log F + 10 log F) with individual heap insertions for F relevant users; O(posts+follow edges) persistent storage.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • A user always sees their own posts
  • Following the same user twice must not duplicate tweets
  • Unfollowing removes that user’s posts from later feeds

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0300-0399/0355.Design%20Twitter/Solution.py

class Twitter:
    def __init__(self):
        """
        Initialize your data structure here.
        """
        self.user_tweets = defaultdict(list)
        self.user_following = defaultdict(set)
        self.tweets = defaultdict()
        self.time = 0

    def postTweet(self, userId: int, tweetId: int) -> None:
        """
        Compose a new tweet.
        """
        self.time += 1
        self.user_tweets[userId].append(tweetId)
        self.tweets[tweetId] = self.time

    def getNewsFeed(self, userId: int) -> List[int]:
        """
        Retrieve the 10 most recent tweet ids in the user's news feed. Each item in the news feed must be posted by users who the user followed or by the user herself. Tweets must be ordered from most recent to least recent.
        """
        following = self.user_following[userId]
        users = set(following)
        users.add(userId)
        tweets = [self.user_tweets[u][::-1][:10] for u in users]
        tweets = sum(tweets, [])
        return nlargest(10, tweets, key=lambda tweet: self.tweets[tweet])

    def follow(self, followerId: int, followeeId: int) -> None:
        """
        Follower follows a followee. If the operation is invalid, it should be a no-op.
        """
        self.user_following[followerId].add(followeeId)

    def unfollow(self, followerId: int, followeeId: int) -> None:
        """
        Follower unfollows a followee. If the operation is invalid, it should be a no-op.
        """
        following = self.user_following[followerId]
        if followeeId in following:
            following.remove(followeeId)

cards.title: Combination Sum IV
cards.summary: Count ordered sequences of allowed positive values that add to a target; different orders count separately.
cards.question:
Count ordered sequences of allowed positive values that add to a target; different orders count separately.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Let dp[t] count sequences totaling t, with one empty sequence for total zero. For each total in ascending order, consider every possible final value and add dp[t−value]; putting totals in the outer loop counts orderings correctly.

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0400-0499/0417.Pacific%20Atlantic%20Water%20Flow/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def pacificAtlantic(self, heights: List[List[int]]) -> List[List[int]]:
        def bfs(q: Deque[Tuple[int, int]], vis: List[List[bool]]) -> None:
            while q:
                x, y = q.popleft()
                for dx, dy in pairwise(dirs):
                    nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
                    if (
                        0 <= nx < m
                        and 0 <= ny < n
                        and not vis[nx][ny]
                        and heights[nx][ny] >= heights[x][y]
                    ):
                        vis[nx][ny] = True
                        q.append((nx, ny))

        m, n = len(heights), len(heights[0])
        vis1 = [[False] * n for _ in range(m)]
        vis2 = [[False] * n for _ in range(m)]
        q1: Deque[Tuple[int, int]] = deque()
        q2: Deque[Tuple[int, int]] = deque()
        dirs = (-1, 0, 1, 0, -1)

        for i in range(m):
            q1.append((i, 0))
            vis1[i][0] = True
            q2.append((i, n - 1))
            vis2[i][n - 1] = True

        for j in range(n):
            q1.append((0, j))
            vis1[0][j] = True
            q2.append((m - 1, j))
            vis2[m - 1][j] = True

        bfs(q1, vis1)
        bfs(q2, vis2)

        return [[i, j] for i in range(m) for j in range(n) if vis1[i][j] and vis2[i][j]]

cards.question:
Represent a binary square grid as a quadtree whose leaves describe uniform regions.

cards.question:

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0400-0499/0437.Path%20Sum%20III/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def pathSum(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], targetSum: int) -> int:
        def dfs(node, s):
            if node is None:
                return 0
            s += node.val
            ans = cnt[s - targetSum]
            cnt[s] += 1
            ans += dfs(node.left, s)
            ans += dfs(node.right, s)
            cnt[s] -= 1
            return ans

        cnt = Counter({0: 1})
        return dfs(root, 0)

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0400-0499/0450.Delete%20Node%20in%20a%20BST/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def deleteNode(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], key: int) -> Optional[TreeNode]:
        if root is None:
            return None
        if root.val > key:
            root.left = self.deleteNode(root.left, key)
            return root
        if root.val < key:
            root.right = self.deleteNode(root.right, key)
            return root
        if root.left is None:
            return root.right
        if root.right is None:
            return root.left
        node = root.right
        while node.left:
            node = node.left
        node.left = root.left
        root = root.right
        return root

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0400-0499/0460.LFU%20Cache/Solution.py

class Node:
    def __init__(self, key: int, value: int) -> None:
        self.key = key
        self.value = value
        self.freq = 1
        self.prev = None
        self.next = None


class DoublyLinkedList:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.head = Node(-1, -1)
        self.tail = Node(-1, -1)
        self.head.next = self.tail
        self.tail.prev = self.head

    def add_first(self, node: Node) -> None:
        node.prev = self.head
        node.next = self.head.next
        self.head.next.prev = node
        self.head.next = node

    def remove(self, node: Node) -> Node:
        node.next.prev = node.prev
        node.prev.next = node.next
        node.next, node.prev = None, None
        return node

    def remove_last(self) -> Node:
        return self.remove(self.tail.prev)

    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
        return self.head.next == self.tail


class LFUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.min_freq = 0
        self.map = defaultdict(Node)
        self.freq_map = defaultdict(DoublyLinkedList)

    def get(self, key: int) -> int:
        if self.capacity == 0 or key not in self.map:
            return -1
        node = self.map[key]
        self.incr_freq(node)
        return node.value

    def put(self, key: int, value: int) -> None:
        if self.capacity == 0:
            return
        if key in self.map:
            node = self.map[key]
            node.value = value
            self.incr_freq(node)
            return
        if len(self.map) == self.capacity:
            ls = self.freq_map[self.min_freq]
            node = ls.remove_last()
            self.map.pop(node.key)
        node = Node(key, value)
        self.add_node(node)
        self.map[key] = node
        self.min_freq = 1

    def incr_freq(self, node: Node) -> None:
        freq = node.freq
        ls = self.freq_map[freq]
        ls.remove(node)
        if ls.is_empty():
            self.freq_map.pop(freq)
            if freq == self.min_freq:
                self.min_freq += 1
        node.freq += 1
        self.add_node(node)

    def add_node(self, node: Node) -> None:
        freq = node.freq
        ls = self.freq_map[freq]
        ls.add_first(node)
        self.freq_map[freq] = ls

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def getMinimumDifference(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
        def dfs(root: Optional[TreeNode]):
            if root is None:
                return
            dfs(root.left)
            nonlocal pre, ans
            ans = min(ans, root.val - pre)
            pre = root.val
            dfs(root.right)

        pre = -inf
        ans = inf
        dfs(root)
        return ans

#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def diameterOfBinaryTree(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
        def dfs(root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
            if root is None:
                return 0
            l, r = dfs(root.left), dfs(root.right)
            nonlocal ans
            ans = max(ans, l + r)
            return 1 + max(l, r)

        ans = 0
        dfs(root)
        return ans

cards.question:
Count contiguous, nonempty ranges whose values add to a chosen target, including inputs containing negative numbers.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Track the running prefix sum and how often each earlier prefix occurred. A current sum s completes one range for every earlier prefix s−target; query before recording s so empty ranges are not counted.

Target complexity

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0500-0599/0560.Subarray%20Sum%20Equals%20K/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def subarraySum(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        cnt = Counter({0: 1})
        ans = s = 0
        for x in nums:
            s += x
            ans += cnt[s - k]
            cnt[s] += 1
        return ans

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0600-0699/0622.Design%20Circular%20Queue/Solution.py

class MyCircularQueue:
    def __init__(self, k: int):
        self.q = [0] * k
        self.size = 0
        self.capacity = k
        self.front = 0

    def enQueue(self, value: int) -> bool:
        if self.isFull():
            return False
        self.q[(self.front + self.size) % self.capacity] = value
        self.size += 1
        return True

    def deQueue(self) -> bool:
        if self.isEmpty():
            return False
        self.front = (self.front + 1) % self.capacity
        self.size -= 1
        return True

    def Front(self) -> int:
        return -1 if self.isEmpty() else self.q[self.front]

    def Rear(self) -> int:
        if self.isEmpty():
            return -1
        return self.q[(self.front + self.size - 1) % self.capacity]

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == 0

    def isFull(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == self.capacity


# Your MyCircularQueue object will be instantiated and called as such:
# obj = MyCircularQueue(k)
# param_1 = obj.enQueue(value)
# param_2 = obj.deQueue()
# param_3 = obj.Front()
# param_4 = obj.Rear()
# param_5 = obj.isEmpty()
# param_6 = obj.isFull()

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0600-0699/0637.Average%20of%20Levels%20in%20Binary%20Tree/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def averageOfLevels(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> List[float]:
        q = deque([root])
        ans = []
        while q:
            s, n = 0, len(q)
            for _ in range(n):
                root = q.popleft()
                s += root.val
                if root.left:
                    q.append(root.left)
                if root.right:
                    q.append(root.right)
            ans.append(s / n)
        return ans

cards.title: Dota2 Senate
cards.summary: Predict which faction wins a cyclic voting process when each active participant can remove an opponent from future turns.
cards.question:
Predict which faction wins a cyclic voting process when each active participant can remove an opponent from future turns.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Keep each faction’s surviving turn positions in an increasing queue. Compare the two earliest positions: the earlier participant bans the other and returns at its position plus the cycle length, preserving chronological order for the next round.

Target complexity

O(n) queue operations and O(n) space with O(1) deque operations; repeated front removal from a plain array can make an implementation slower.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • Only one faction is present.
  • One faction has an early turn but fewer participants.
  • The decisive ban occurs after wrapping into another cycle.

cards.title: Find K Closest Elements
cards.summary: Select k values nearest to a target from a sorted array, preferring the smaller value on equal distance and returning sorted output.
cards.question:
Select k values nearest to a target from a sorted array, preferring the smaller value on equal distance and returning sorted output.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

The answer occupies a contiguous length-k window. Binary-search its starting index by comparing the value that would leave on the left with the value that would enter on the right; ties keep the left window.

Target complexity

O(log(n−k+1) + k) time including output and O(k) output space; the search itself uses O(1) space.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • The target lies outside the array range.
  • Distances tie on both sides of the target.
  • k equals the entire array length.

cards.title: Valid Parenthesis String
cards.summary: Check whether a string can become balanced parentheses when each star may stand for an opener, a closer, or nothing.
cards.question:
Check whether a string can become balanced parentheses when each star may stand for an opener, a closer, or nothing.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Track the smallest and largest feasible count of unmatched opening parentheses for each prefix. Reject if even the largest count becomes negative, clamp the smallest at zero, and accept only if zero remains feasible at the end.

Target complexity

O(n) time and O(1) space; the interval of possible balances replaces exponential assignment search.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • "*" → true
  • "(*))" → true
  • ")*" → false

Compare from both ends until the first mismatch. At that point the only useful choices are to skip the left character or the right character, then check the remaining interval without permitting another deletion.

  • Only one of the two mismatch deletions works.
  • Two separated mismatches make one deletion insufficient.

cards.title: Redundant Connection
cards.summary: Find the extra edge whose removal restores an undirected graph formed by adding one edge to a tree.
cards.question:
Find the extra edge whose removal restores an undirected graph formed by adding one edge to a tree.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Process edges in input order with disjoint-set union. An edge whose endpoints already share a representative closes the unique cycle; it is the last edge of that cycle encountered in input order.

Target complexity

O(E·α(V)) amortized time and O(V) space with path compression and union by size/rank.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • Triangle edges return the edge that closes the triangle
  • The extra edge need not be the final input edge
  • Vertices may already be indirectly connected by several edges

cards.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
cards.summary: Partition all positive values into k nonempty groups with identical sums.
cards.question:
Partition all positive values into k nonempty groups with identical sums.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

First check divisibility and the largest-value bound. A bitmask DP can record the current bucket’s partial sum for each used-position mask: add an unused value only if it fits, and reset the partial sum to zero whenever a bucket is completed.

Target complexity

O(n × 2^n) time and O(2^n) space for bitmask DP; backtracking alternatives instead have exponential search with different pruning costs.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • k is one or equals the number of values.
  • The total is divisible but no valid partition exists.
  • Repeated values create many equivalent choices.

Compare the target with the current node and follow only the side that can contain it. Stop at an exact match or a missing child; the search-tree ordering makes exploring the other branch unnecessary.

Target complexity

  • The target is the root value.
  • The target is absent.
  • A skewed tree behaves like a linked list.

cards.question:

Keep a min heap containing only the largest k values encountered so far. Insert each new value and discard the minimum when the heap grows past k; the retained minimum is the kth largest.

cards.title: Design HashSet
cards.summary: Implement integer-set membership, insertion, and removal without using a built-in set.
cards.question:
Implement integer-set membership, insertion, and removal without using a built-in set.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

For a bounded key universe, a direct-address boolean array gives an especially clear implementation. Alternatively, hash into buckets and scan only a collision chain; deduplicate insertions and make removal of an absent key harmless.

Direct addressing: O(1) operations and O(U) space for universe U. Resized chaining: expected O(1), worst-case O(n); a list-only implementation instead has O(n) operations.

cards.question:
Implement a key-value map with replacement, lookup, and removal, including the required missing-key result.

Hash each key to a bucket and store collision-chain entries containing both the key and value. Search for an existing key before appending; replacement changes its value, and deletion reconnects its neighbors.

  • Remove the first or last item in a collision chain.

cards.title: Asteroid Collision
cards.summary: Resolve collisions among signed moving objects on a line, keeping the survivors in their original spatial order.
cards.question:
Resolve collisions among signed moving objects on a line, keeping the survivors in their original spatial order.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Keep survivors on a stack and process each new object against the stack top only when the top moves right and the newcomer moves left. Repeatedly remove the smaller magnitude, discard both on a tie, and continue until the newcomer is gone or no collision remains.

Target complexity

O(n) amortized time and O(n) stack space, since each object is pushed and removed at most once.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • Equal magnitudes destroy each other.
  • One large left-moving object destroys several earlier objects.
  • Objects moving away from each other never collide.

Find the least cost to reach just beyond a staircase, paying for each step used and moving one or two steps at a time.

How to approach it

For each step, compute its own cost plus the cheaper cost-to-finish of the next two steps. The answer is the better result from starting at step zero or step one; rolling states can avoid mutating the input.

O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; a backward DP may overwrite the input, while rolling states preserve it.

cards.title: Open the Lock
cards.summary: Find the fewest wheel turns needed to reach a combination while never entering forbidden combinations.
cards.question:
Find the fewest wheel turns needed to reach a combination while never entering forbidden combinations.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Treat each combination as a graph vertex and each single-wheel increment or decrement as an edge. Breadth-first search from the initial combination gives minimum turns; exclude forbidden vertices and mark states when enqueued.

Target complexity

For four decimal wheels, at most 10,000 states with eight neighbors each: O(10⁴ + d) time/space including d forbidden entries, treating four-character operations as constant.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • The initial combination is forbidden.
  • The target equals the initial combination.
  • Wheel rotation wraps between nine and zero.

cards.question:
Split a string into as many contiguous parts as possible so each character occurs in only one part.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Record the last index of every character. While scanning a part, extend its required end to the latest last occurrence seen, and cut exactly when the scan reaches that end.

Target complexity

O(n) time and O(u) last-position space plus output; u is at most 26 for the stated alphabet.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • "aaaa" → one part of length 4
  • "abc" → [1,1,1]
  • "abac" → [3,1]

cards.title: Reorganize String
cards.summary: Rearrange a string so equal characters never occupy adjacent positions, or report that no arrangement exists.
cards.question:
Rearrange a string so equal characters never occupy adjacent positions, or report that no arrangement exists.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Count remaining characters and repeatedly select the most frequent eligible character. Temporarily withhold the previously used character from the max-heap, returning it only after another character is chosen; if only the withheld character remains, completion is impossible.

Target complexity

O(n log σ) time with σ distinct characters and O(σ) heap state plus O(n) output; use a buffer to avoid quadratic string copying.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • One character occurs more than half the rounded-up length.
  • All characters are distinct.
  • A valid result exists exactly at the frequency feasibility boundary.

cards.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
cards.summary: Find the cheapest flight route using at most k intermediate stops, or return -1 if no such route exists.
cards.question:
Find the cheapest flight route using at most k intermediate stops, or return -1 if no such route exists.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Perform k+1 rounds of edge relaxation, where each round reads only the previous round’s distance array. Copying the array prevents updates from chaining through too many flights within one round.

Target complexity

O((k+1)(V+E)) time for copied-array Bellman-Ford rounds and O(V) working space; k stops means at most k+1 edges.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • k=0 allows only a direct flight
  • The cheapest unlimited-stop route may be invalid
  • No valid route within the stop budget → -1

cards.title: Domino and Tromino Tiling
cards.summary: Count tilings of a two-row board using dominoes and L-shaped trominoes, modulo the required modulus.
cards.question:
Count tilings of a two-row board using dominoes and L-shaped trominoes, modulo the required modulus.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Use DP states for fully filled prefixes and prefixes with one corner gap; gap states capture the ways trominoes cross a boundary. Eliminating the gap states yields f(n) = 2f(n-1) + f(n-3), starting from f(0)=1, f(1)=1, and f(2)=2.

Target complexity

O(n) time and O(1) rolling-state space for the recurrence; count arithmetic must preserve exact modular values.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • Width one has a single vertical-domino tiling.
  • Width two establishes the two base tilings.
  • Large widths require reducing intermediate counts modulo the specified modulus.

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0700-0799/0790.Domino%20and%20Tromino%20Tiling/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def numTilings(self, n: int) -> int:
        f = [1, 0, 0, 0]
        mod = 10**9 + 7
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            g = [0] * 4
            g[0] = (f[0] + f[1] + f[2] + f[3]) % mod
            g[1] = (f[2] + f[3]) % mod
            g[2] = (f[1] + f[3]) % mod
            g[3] = f[0]
            f = g
        return f[0]

cards.summary: Determine whether a multiset of cards can be divided into equal-sized groups of consecutive values.
cards.question:
Determine whether a multiset of cards can be divided into equal-sized groups of consecutive values.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Always start a group with the smallest remaining card, because no earlier group can absorb it later. Consume one occurrence of every required consecutive value and fail immediately if a value is missing or exhausted out of order.

Target complexity

O(n log u) time and O(u) space with a heap or sorted distinct keys, where u is the number of distinct card values.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • Card count not divisible by group size → false
  • Group size 1 always succeeds
  • [1,2,3,3,4,5], group size 3 → true

cards.summary: Count how many groups of cars reach a common target when cars cannot pass and a catching car joins the slower group ahead.
cards.question:
Count how many groups of cars reach a common target when cars cannot pass and a catching car joins the slower group ahead.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0800-0899/0872.Leaf-Similar%20Trees/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def leafSimilar(self, root1: Optional[TreeNode], root2: Optional[TreeNode]) -> bool:
        def dfs(root: Optional[TreeNode], nums: List[int]) -> None:
            if root.left == root.right:
                nums.append(root.val)
                return
            if root.left:
                dfs(root.left, nums)
            if root.right:
                dfs(root.right, nums)

        l1, l2 = [], []
        dfs(root1, l1)
        dfs(root2, l2)
        return l1 == l2

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0800-0899/0895.Maximum%20Frequency%20Stack/Solution.py

class FreqStack:
    def __init__(self):
        self.cnt = defaultdict(int)
        self.q = []
        self.ts = 0

    def push(self, val: int) -> None:
        self.ts += 1
        self.cnt[val] += 1
        heappush(self.q, (-self.cnt[val], -self.ts, val))

    def pop(self) -> int:
        val = heappop(self.q)[2]
        self.cnt[val] -= 1
        return val


# Your FreqStack object will be instantiated and called as such:
# obj = FreqStack()

class StockSpanner:
    def __init__(self):
        self.stk = []

    def next(self, price: int) -> int:
        cnt = 1
        while self.stk and self.stk[-1][0] <= price:
            cnt += self.stk.pop()[1]
        self.stk.append((price, cnt))

Sort an integer array without delegating the work to a built-in sorting function.

Merge sort divides the range into halves, recursively sorts each half, and merges them with two read pointers. During merging, the output prefix always contains the smallest already consumed values in order.

Target complexity

  • Several values are equal.

cards.summary: Find the largest sum of a nonempty contiguous block when an array is considered circular and no position may be used twice.

Find the largest sum of a nonempty contiguous block when an array is considered circular and no position may be used twice.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Compute the best ordinary subarray and the smallest ordinary subarray alongside the total sum. A wrapping answer is the total minus a minimum middle block; when every value is negative, use the ordinary maximum instead of accidentally selecting an empty complement.

Target complexity

O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space using maximum and minimum Kadane scans.

  • The best block wraps across the last and first positions.
  • The whole array is optimal or there is a single element.

cards.title: Number of Recent Calls
cards.summary: Maintain a count of calls within a trailing time window as timestamps arrive in increasing order.
cards.question:
Maintain a count of calls within a trailing time window as timestamps arrive in increasing order.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Append each new timestamp to a queue, then remove timestamps strictly older than t-3000. The remaining queue represents the inclusive interval ending at the current call; monotone arrival times guarantee expired calls never become relevant again.

Target complexity

O(1) amortized work per call with a queue and O(window population) storage; repeated array shifts can violate the time target.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • A call exactly 3000 units old still counts.
  • A long gap expires every earlier call.
  • Many closely spaced calls remain in the window.

Map each character to its rank and compare each neighboring pair of words. The first unequal character determines order; if all compared characters agree, the shorter word must come first.

cards.summary: Find the longest contiguous interval whose neighboring comparisons alternate between rising and falling.
cards.question:
Find the longest contiguous interval whose neighboring comparisons alternate between rising and falling.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Track the sign of the previous unequal comparison and the current alternating-run length. Extend only when the sign flips; equality resets the run to one, while a repeated sign starts a new two-element candidate.

Target complexity

O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary state.

  • Two adjacent values are equal.
  • The array is strictly increasing.
  • A long alternating run begins after an early reset.

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0900-0999/0978.Longest%20Turbulent%20Subarray/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def maxTurbulenceSize(self, arr: List[int]) -> int:
        ans = f = g = 1
        for a, b in pairwise(arr):
            ff = g + 1 if a < b else 1
            gg = f + 1 if a > b else 1
            f, g = ff, gg
            ans = max(ans, f, g)
        return ans

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/0900-0999/0981.Time%20Based%20Key-Value%20Store/Solution.py

class TimeMap:
    def __init__(self):
        self.ktv = defaultdict(list)

    def set(self, key: str, value: str, timestamp: int) -> None:
        self.ktv[key].append((timestamp, value))

    def get(self, key: str, timestamp: int) -> str:
        if key not in self.ktv:
            return ''
        tv = self.ktv[key]
        i = bisect_right(tv, (timestamp, chr(127)))
        return tv[i - 1][1] if i else ''

cards.question:

For each directed trust edge, subtract one from its source’s balance and add one to its destination’s balance. Under the distinct-edge contract, only a person with balance n−1 can have every required incoming edge and no outgoing edge.

  • A popular person trusts somebody else.
  • No person receives trust from every other person.

Expand a sliding window while counting its zeroes. Whenever the count exceeds k, advance the left boundary until the budget is restored; record the length only for a window satisfying the zero budget.

cards.question:
Find the smallest ship capacity that can transport ordered package weights within a day limit, without splitting packages.

cards.answer:
How to approach it

For any proposed capacity, greedily load each day until the next package would exceed it. The required day count decreases monotonically as capacity grows, so binary-search between the heaviest package and the total weight.

Target complexity

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

  • A package exactly fills the current day’s capacity.

cards.title: Last Stone Weight II
cards.summary: Choose a sequence of pairwise stone reductions that leaves the smallest possible final weight.
cards.question:
Choose a sequence of pairwise stone reductions that leaves the smallest possible final weight.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

View the reductions as assigning each original weight to one of two opposing totals. Find a reachable subset sum as close as possible to half the total, then minimize the difference between that sum and the remainder.

Target complexity

O(nS) time and O(S) space for a one-dimensional subset-sum DP with total weight S; memoized index-and-sum variants use O(nS) states.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • An exact equal partition leaves zero weight.
  • One stone is larger than all others combined.
  • Repeated weights must each be usable at most once.

cards.title: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings
cards.summary: Find the longest string that can be repeated a whole number of times to form each of two given strings.
cards.question:
Find the longest string that can be repeated a whole number of times to form each of two given strings.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

First verify that concatenating the strings in either order produces the same result; otherwise they have no common repeating base. When compatible, take a prefix whose length is the greatest common divisor of the two lengths.

Target complexity

O(m+n) time and O(m+n) temporary space for concatenation-based checking; a character-wise check can reduce working space. Checking every possible divisor length has a higher bound.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • The strings have compatible lengths but different repeated content.
  • One string is several copies of the other.
  • The common base contains more than one distinct character.

  • Several trips overlap at the capacity limit.
  • One trip alone exceeds capacity.

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/1100-1199/1161.Maximum%20Level%20Sum%20of%20a%20Binary%20Tree/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def maxLevelSum(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
        q = deque([root])
        mx = -inf
        i = 0
        while q:
            i += 1
            s = 0
            for _ in range(len(q)):
                node = q.popleft()
                s += node.val
                if node.left:
                    q.append(node.left)
                if node.right:
                    q.append(node.right)
            if mx < s:
                mx = s
                ans = i
        return ans

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/1300-1399/1325.Delete%20Leaves%20With%20a%20Given%20Value/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def removeLeafNodes(
        self, root: Optional[TreeNode], target: int
    ) -> Optional[TreeNode]:
        if root is None:
            return None
        root.left = self.removeLeafNodes(root.left, target)
        root.right = self.removeLeafNodes(root.right, target)
        if root.left is None and root.right is None and root.val == target:
            return None
        return root

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/1300-1399/1372.Longest%20ZigZag%20Path%20in%20a%20Binary%20Tree/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def longestZigZag(self, root: TreeNode) -> int:
        def dfs(root, l, r):
            if root is None:
                return
            nonlocal ans
            ans = max(ans, l, r)
            dfs(root.left, r + 1, 0)
            dfs(root.right, 0, l + 1)

        ans = 0
        dfs(root, 0, 0)
        return ans

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/1400-1499/1448.Count%20Good%20Nodes%20in%20Binary%20Tree/Solution.py

# Definition for a binary tree node.
# class TreeNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.left = left
#         self.right = right
class Solution:
    def goodNodes(self, root: TreeNode) -> int:
        def dfs(root: TreeNode, mx: int):
            if root is None:
                return
            nonlocal ans
            if mx <= root.val:
                ans += 1
                mx = root.val
            dfs(root.left, mx)
            dfs(root.right, mx)

        ans = 0
        dfs(root, -1000000)
        return ans

cards.summary: Answer whether one course is a direct or indirect prerequisite of another for many queries.
cards.question:
Answer whether one course is a direct or indirect prerequisite of another for many queries.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.

Precompute reachability rather than repeating a full traversal for every query. A clear baseline uses a boolean transitive-closure matrix: for each possible intermediate course, connect every predecessor to every successor, then answer each query by lookup.

Target complexity

O(v³ + q) time and O(v²) space for closure and q queries; DAG-specific propagation can improve this, while memoized set unions have different costs.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

  • A prerequisite chain contains several intermediate courses.
  • Two courses are unrelated.
  • One course is a prerequisite through multiple different paths.

cards.summary: Classify graph edges as required in every minimum spanning tree or usable in at least one such tree without being required.
cards.question:

Maintain a sliding window containing at most one zero. Its usable length is window length minus one, which accounts for deleting the zero or, in an all-one window, deleting a one as the problem still requires.

Target complexity

O(n) time and O(1) extra space; exactly one deletion distinguishes this from an at-most-one-flip problem.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

  • An all-one array returns its length minus one.
  • A single-element array becomes empty.
  • Two zeroes force the left boundary to move.

Use Dijkstra’s frontier, but combine a route cost with an edge using max rather than addition. An improved candidate is max(current effort, edge difference), and the first finalized destination has the smallest achievable worst step.

Target complexity

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

  • A one-cell grid needs no effort.
  • A longer route avoids one steep direct step.
  • Many routes share the same maximum edge cost.

cards.title: Single-Threaded CPU
cards.summary: Simulate a processor that chooses the shortest available task, breaking ties by original task index, and return its execution order.
cards.question:
Simulate a processor that chooses the shortest available task, breaking ties by original task index, and return its execution order.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Sort tasks by release time and place available tasks in a min-heap keyed by duration and original index. After each completion, add newly released tasks; if no task is available, jump directly to the next release time.

Target complexity

O(n log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space; accumulated simulation time may require a wider integer type.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • The processor is idle between task batches.
  • Several tasks have the same processing time.
  • Tasks arrive while a long task is running.

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/1800-1899/1834.Single-Threaded%20CPU/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def getOrder(self, tasks: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        for i, task in enumerate(tasks):
            task.append(i)
        tasks.sort()
        ans = []
        q = []
        n = len(tasks)
        i = t = 0
        while q or i < n:
            if not q:
                t = max(t, tasks[i][0])
            while i < n and tasks[i][0] <= t:
                heappush(q, (tasks[i][1], tasks[i][2]))
                i += 1
            pt, j = heappop(q)
            ans.append(j)
            t += pt
        return ans

cards.question:

Let reachable[i] depend on whether any reachable predecessor lies from i−maxJump through i−minJump. Maintain the count of such predecessors as a sliding window, adding and expiring one position per step instead of checking every possible jump.

Target complexity

O(n) time and O(n) reachability storage; a bounded circular buffer can reduce stored history when the maximum jump is small.

  • minJump equals maxJump.

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/1800-1899/1871.Jump%20Game%20VII/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def canReach(self, s: str, minJump: int, maxJump: int) -> bool:
        n = len(s)
        pre = [0] * (n + 1)
        pre[1] = 1
        f = [True] + [False] * (n - 1)
        for i in range(1, n):
            if s[i] == "0":
                l, r = max(0, i - maxJump), i - minJump
                f[i] = l <= r and pre[r + 1] - pre[l] > 0
            pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + f[i]
        return f[-1]

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/2000-2099/2095.Delete%20the%20Middle%20Node%20of%20a%20Linked%20List/Solution.py

# Definition for singly-linked list.
# class ListNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.next = next
class Solution:
    def deleteMiddle(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        dummy = ListNode(next=head)
        slow, fast = dummy, head
        while fast and fast.next:
            slow = slow.next
            fast = fast.next.next
        slow.next = slow.next.next
        return dummy.next

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/2100-2199/2130.Maximum%20Twin%20Sum%20of%20a%20Linked%20List/Solution.py

# Definition for singly-linked list.
# class ListNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.next = next
class Solution:
    def pairSum(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> int:
        s = []
        while head:
            s.append(head.val)
            head = head.next
        n = len(s)
        return max(s[i] + s[-(i + 1)] for i in range(n >> 1))

Keep a frontier for the smallest never-removed integer and a min-heap for smaller values that were added back. A companion membership set prevents duplicate heap entries; pop from the heap when possible, otherwise return and advance the frontier.

cards.summary: Place each value from 1 through k once in a square matrix so separate above/below and left/right constraints are satisfied.
cards.question:
Place each value from 1 through k once in a square matrix so separate above/below and left/right constraints are satisfied.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Topologically sort the row constraints and the column constraints independently. A cycle in either makes placement impossible; otherwise each value receives its row position from the first order and its column position from the second, with all unused cells zero.

Target complexity

O(k²+r+c) time including the output matrix, and O(k+r+c) working space plus O(k²) output for r row edges and c column edges.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

  • Repeated precedence edges must be handled consistently.

cards.title: Total Cost to Hire K Workers
cards.summary: Hire k workers by repeatedly choosing the lowest-cost eligible worker from the first or last candidate windows of the remaining list.
cards.question:
Hire k workers by repeatedly choosing the lowest-cost eligible worker from the first or last candidate windows of the remaining list.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Maintain disjoint left and right frontiers and a heap of eligible workers keyed by cost then original index. After removing a worker, refill from that same side if an unseen worker remains, taking care not to insert the overlapping middle region twice.

Target complexity

Let h = min(n, 2c) for candidate-window size c: O(h + k log(h + 1)) time with heapify and O(h) space; repeated sorting of candidates is slower.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • The two candidate windows overlap from the beginning.
  • Equal costs are resolved by the smaller original index.
  • k includes every worker.

cards.title: Maximum Subsequence Score
cards.summary: Choose k shared indices to maximize a first-array sum multiplied by the smallest chosen second-array value.
cards.question:
Choose k shared indices to maximize a first-array sum multiplied by the smallest chosen second-array value.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Sort paired values by the second array in descending order and retain the best k-1 earlier first-array values in a min-heap. Add the current value, evaluate its second value times the sum when k items are present, then discard the smallest first-array value for the next iteration; each evaluation explicitly includes the current minimum.

Target complexity

O(n log n + n log k) time and O(n + k) storage for paired sorting and the heap; use a numeric type that preserves the largest score exactly.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • k = 1 reduces the choice to individual paired products.
  • k equals the full array length.
  • Equal second-array values can arrive in any order.

python.code:
# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/2500-2599/2542.Maximum%20Subsequence%20Score/Solution.py

class Solution:
    def maxScore(self, nums1: List[int], nums2: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        nums = sorted(zip(nums2, nums1), reverse=True)
        q = []
        ans = s = 0
        for a, b in nums:
            s += b
            heappush(q, b)
            if len(q) == k:
                ans = max(ans, s * a)
                s -= heappop(q)
        return ans

Factor each value and associate each prime factor with one previously seen index. Union indices that share a prime factor instead of checking every pair, then test whether all indices have the same representative.

# Doocs contributors · CC-BY-SA-4.0
# Source: https://github.com/doocs/leetcode/blob/88c8c2c29f19c186d7cc05c9db17245d9ae3df43/solution/2800-2899/2807.Insert%20Greatest%20Common%20Divisors%20in%20Linked%20List/Solution.py

# Definition for singly-linked list.
# class ListNode:
#     def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
#         self.val = val
#         self.next = next
class Solution:
    def insertGreatestCommonDivisors(
        self, head: Optional[ListNode]
    ) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        pre, cur = head, head.next
        while cur:
            x = gcd(pre.val, cur.val)
            pre.next = ListNode(x, cur)
            pre, cur = cur, cur.next
        return head

cards.title: Minimum Array End
cards.summary: Minimize the final value of an increasing positive array of length n whose combined bitwise AND is x.
cards.question:
Minimize the final value of an increasing positive array of length n whose combined bitwise AND is x.

Independent study brief. Open the official problem for the complete constraints and judge examples.
cards.answer:
How to approach it

Every chosen value must include all set bits of x, so start with x and treat its zero-bit positions as free digits. Deposit the binary digits of n−1 into those zero positions from low to high; this selects the nth smallest permitted value without constructing the whole array.

Target complexity

O(log n + log x) bit-position steps with fixed-width arithmetic; use BigInt for wide JavaScript results and account for bit-operation cost with arbitrary precision.

These bounds describe the target approach above. Compare the reference implementation’s data structures and copying costs before assigning it the same bounds.

Cases to walk through

  • n is one, so the answer is x.
  • The low bits of x are all set, forcing new bits higher up.
  • The result exceeds the safe range of 32-bit JavaScript bitwise arithmetic.
